findings.title: Ops rail/global pause not enforced at the irreversible settlement boundary
findings.description: assertRailActive() is called only at the top of some routes. The public facilitator settle route, account funding, the x402 paywall and MPP reach defaultSettler() without any pause check, and a request that passed a route-top check before a pause landed still settles (TOCTOU). An operator pausing in an incident would believe broadcasting had stopped when it had not.
findings.preconditions: On-chain settlement live (ONCHAIN_SETTLEMENT_LIVE on, KMS configured) and an incident in progress.
findings.evidence: grep of assertRailActive callers, 2026-10-03; facilitator/settle/route.ts has no pause check.
findings.rationale_for_severity: Bypass of a secondary safeguard (containment control). Not P1: production settlement is gated off by ONCHAIN_SETTLEMENT_LIVE/KMS today, and the bypass needs an incident to matter.
findings.remediation: Settlement safety gate inside the settler (beforeBroadcast) checking the durable breaker AND the ops global pause, failing closed.
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: 'the ops console's global pause stops the settler', '10/11 halt raised mid-flight'
findings.retest: 30/30 safety spec pass; residual: rail-scope pauses remain route-level by design (settler cannot tell which rail called it)
findings.residual_risk: Rail-scope pause still does not stop the facilitator route; use a network or global halt.

findings.title: Emergency control state fails open on store read errors
findings.description: controls.ts deliberately does not fail closed when Redis cannot be read. Correct for quotes; wrong for broadcasts.
findings.preconditions: Redis outage during an active pause.
findings.evidence: Module header comment and readFlag implementation.
findings.remediation: Settler-side gate fails closed on any read error (state, epoch, ops pause, velocity counter).
findings.status: fixed for the settlement path (pending deploy); route-level behaviour unchanged by design
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: '20. an unreadable control plane refuses settlement'
findings.residual_risk: Quote routes still fail open on a control-plane outage (intended).

findings.title: RPC chain identity not verified before signing with local/KMS accounts
findings.description: viem asserts the RPC's chain id only for json-rpc accounts. For local and KMS accounts it signs for the configured chain and then trusts receipts from whatever the RPC is. A misconfigured or wrong-network RPC would have its receipts treated as settlement evidence.
findings.evidence: node_modules/viem/_esm/actions/wallet/sendTransaction.js: assertCurrentChain only in the json-rpc branch.
findings.validation: confirmed by reading the library source
findings.remediation: Probe eth_chainId on every configured provider before signing; mismatch halts the network.
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: '2. a wrong chain id refuses the request and halts the network'
findings.residual_risk: A provider that lies consistently about everything is not detectable with one provider (FP-SET-06).

findings.title: Settlement success relied on receipt status alone
findings.description: A `success` receipt was reported as settled without checking that it contained exactly the authorized Transfer and AuthorizationUsed events. Exploitation requires the pinned token contract to misbehave (upgrade) or the RPC to serve a different receipt.
findings.preconditions: Token contract upgrade or lying RPC.
findings.remediation: verifySettlementReceipt; mismatch halts the network and surfaces as SettlementPendingError so every caller records the tx unresolved.

findings.title: No per-network index of unresolved settlements; no reorg re-check of confirmed ones
findings.description: Settlement records were keyed only by tx hash, so nothing could enumerate pending/abandoned settlements or re-check recent confirmations for reorgs.
findings.remediation: Sorted-set indexes maintained in recordSettlement; reconcileNetwork() pass; recovery blocked while any are unresolved. Round 2: scheduled sweep (lib/settlementSweep.ts, GET /api/cron/settlement-safety, requireCron + runJob lock/budget/record), daily Vercel cron as backstop, external scheduler supported via FURLPAY_CRON_SECRET.
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts reconciliation block; settlementHardening.spec.ts 'scheduled sweep' block
findings.residual_risk: Vercel cron is daily: a backstop, not a monitor. Sub-hourly cadence needs an external scheduler (founder/ops decision). Records written before the index existed are not indexed.

findings.title: Single-RPC deployments cannot detect provider disagreement
findings.description: With one provider, a consistently lying or forked RPC is undetectable. Whether production has a fallback configured could not be verified from the repository.
findings.preconditions: Only one RPC configured for a settlement network.
findings.validation: confirmed: production defines no ARBITRUM_RPC_URL or fallback, so the settler would use viem's single public endpoint
findings.remediation: Configure an independent second provider per settlement network. The probe reports `rpc_unverified` until then. Round 2: evaluateRpcIndependence() reports two configured URLs on one domain as rpc_not_independent.
findings.owner: founder/ops: configure ARBITRUM_RPC_URL and ARBITRUM_RPC_URL_FALLBACK from two different providers before enabling settlement
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: 'a single provider is reported as unverified'
findings.production_exposure: none today (settlement off in production); applies the moment ONCHAIN_SETTLEMENT_LIVE is enabled

history.note: PN -> P3: validated against production env names.

findings.title: No detection of USDC proxy implementation changes
findings.description: The allowlist pins token addresses but not their implementation. FP-SET-04's receipt check covers misbehaviour after an upgrade; watching the FiatToken proxy Upgraded event would give earlier warning.
findings.remediation: lib/settlementTokenMonitor.ts pins implementation, proxy admin and owner per token; checks paused. Implementation/admin change -> critical halt; owner change -> high halt; paused or unreadable -> degrade. Run by the scheduled sweep and by every recovery check. A test fails if an allowlisted mainnet asset has no pin.
findings.residual_risk: Detection latency = sweep cadence (daily unless an external scheduler is configured). A legitimate issuer upgrade halts the network until a reviewed commit updates the pin. FiatToken role holders below owner (pauser, blacklister, masterMinter) are not pinned.
findings.evidence: On-chain read 2026-10-03: all four pinned tokens (USDC arbitrum/base/polygon, XSGD arbitrum) use ZeppelinOS AdminUpgradeabilityProxy slots; EIP-1967 slots are empty. owner()/paused() readable on all four.

findings.title: Gasless transfers record pending outcomes outside the settlement store
findings.description: On SettlementPendingError the gasless route writes a tx event (recordTxEvent) but not a SettlementRecord, so the reconciler and the recovery gate do not see its unresolved transactions. Round 2 evidence: the route's 202 response pointed clients at /api/x402/settlement/[tx], which returns 404 settlement_not_found for any tx not in the store, so a pending gasless transfer could never be polled.
findings.remediation: Gasless records confirmed and pending outcomes in the settlement store (indexed); a breaker refusal returns 503 settlement_halted instead of 502 + rail DEGRADED.
findings.retest: pass; mutation (pending record removed) fails the test
findings.residual_risk: A disputed gasless tx would not block recovery.

findings.title: No production admin, and a single admin identity cannot satisfy dual approval
findings.description: Round 1: critical recovery needs two distinct approvers and only one account can hold the admin role. Round 2: production defines no FURLPAY_ADMIN_EMAIL at all, so NO account holds the admin role. Manual halt, ops pause/resume and breaker recovery are all unreachable in production. Automatic halts (when enforced) and the env kill switch still work.
findings.remediation: Founder decision: add a second admin identity, or explicitly accept single-operator recovery (not implemented).
findings.owner: founder: (1) set FURLPAY_ADMIN_EMAIL in production; (2) decide how a second approver is provided (second admin identity; role-based admin is not implemented); critical recovery stays fail-closed until then
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: '15. a critical incident needs two distinct approvers'
findings.residual_risk: Operational lock-out after a critical incident.
findings.rationale_for_severity: Raised from P4: the containment controls an operator would use in an incident are unavailable in production, not merely awkward. Not P1: settlement itself is off in production today.

history.note: P4 -> P2 after production env check.

findings.title: Ops resume of a rail/global pause is single-operator with no step-up
findings.description: Resuming a paused rail needs only the admin role and an 8-character reason. No step-up, no second approver. The new settlement breaker has both; the older controls do not.
findings.remediation: Resume (paused=false) on /api/ops/controls requires a fresh step-up claimed atomically (claimStepUp). Pausing does not require step-up, by design.
findings.residual_risk: Resume is still single-operator (no second approver), unlike breaker recovery.

findings.title: Extension service worker trusted all same-id senders, including content scripts
findings.description: Content scripts on every HTTPS page share the extension id; only a static source test kept them from privileged handlers (REVOKE_PASSKEY, LOGOUT, STEP_UP_*, DECLINE_CHALLENGE, RAMP_CHECKOUT). A compromised renderer is not bound by source.
findings.preconditions: Renderer compromise on any open page.
findings.status: fixed (committed d138658; extension not yet published)

findings.title: Elements rangeproof-cache consensus bug (Liquid incident 2026-09-06): FurlPay exposure
findings.source: external advisory: Blockstream incident assessment; CertiK incident analysis
findings.description: Upstream: Elements v0.14.1 to v23.3.3 cached rangeproof/surjection-proof validation under an ambiguous key, allowing unbacked L-BTC issuance; fixed in v23.3.4 (2026-09-09). No CVE ID stated by Blockstream. FurlPay runs no Elements node and has no Liquid asset in any settlement, signing or ledger path; its only Liquid touchpoint is a read-only intel feed whose peg-out observations during the incident window included unbacked flows.
findings.confidence: high for the repository; unknown for partners
findings.validation: repository verified; partner L-BTC acceptance unknown
findings.remediation: None in code. Confirm no partner or treasury counterparty accepts L-BTC on FurlPay's behalf.
findings.residual_risk: Counterparty exposure, if any, is outside FurlPay's control.

findings.title: Compliance-guard wrapper/escrow writes bypassed every settlement control
findings.money_path: PolicyWrapper settleWithPolicy / settleTranche; ComplianceEscrow release / refund (Arbitrum)
findings.description: A second settlement path beside createEvmSettler: payer-signed EIP-3009 authorizations submitted through the PolicyWrapper, and escrow release/refund, signed with FURLPAY_RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY from process env. No circuit breaker, no ops pause, no chain-identity check, no ONCHAIN_SETTLEMENT_LIVE flag, and a raw key allowed in production.
findings.preconditions: Operator credential (requireOperator) and the wrapper/escrow addresses plus relayer key configured.
findings.evidence: grep of writeContract call sites; complianceGuard.walletFor
findings.classification: CWE-693; CWE-321-adjacent (raw key in app env)
findings.rationale_for_severity: Bypass of the settlement containment controls and of the KMS-only custody rule; needs an operator credential and configuration that production does not have today.
findings.production_exposure: none today (no relayer key or wrapper address in production env)
findings.remediation: Money-moving writes call assertMoneyWriteAllowed(): ONCHAIN_SETTLEMENT_LIVE outside development, then beforeBroadcast('arbitrum'). walletFor refuses raw keys in production. Routes map a halt to 503 settlement_halted.
findings.retest: pass; mutation (gate removed) fails the test
findings.residual_risk: Wrapper receipts are not event-verified the way afterReceipt verifies direct EIP-3009 (different event surface). recordSoF attestations (no funds) are not breaker-gated. In production the feature is unavailable until a KMS signer exists.

findings.title: Step-up check-then-consume allowed one re-authentication to authorize concurrent actions
findings.description: recentStepUp() then consumeStepUp() is check-then-delete. Concurrent requests on one session could each pass on a single step-up, e.g. two approvals or two resumes.
findings.validation: confirmed (concurrency test fails without the fix)
findings.remediation: claimStepUp(): SET NX keyed to the step-up's timestamp, then delete. Used by breaker mitigate/approve and controls resume.
findings.regression_test: settlementHardening.spec.ts 'step-up claims are single-use under concurrency'
findings.retest: pass; mutation (NX removed) fails the test
findings.residual_risk: Other routes still use recentStepUp/consumeStepUp (account deletion, offramp, beneficiary); review separately.

findings.title: User-signed transaction relays are outside the breaker (by design)
findings.description: These move the user's own funds under the user's own key. The breaker governs what FurlPay signs and pays gas for; it does not and should not gate a user's wallet. Recorded so the boundary is explicit.
findings.remediation: None. Remove evmAdapter.broadcastTransaction if it stays unused.
findings.residual_risk: During a chain incident FurlPay still relays user-signed transactions.

findings.title: x402 paywall mock path returns a generated tx hash with ok:true
findings.description: When x402LiveMode() is false the paywall returns a random txHash as a successful settlement. x402LiveMode = signatureEnforced(), which lib/x402Enforcement.ts forces on in production (X402_ENFORCE_SIGNATURE cannot disable it there), so the path is unreachable in production.
findings.validation: confirmed by code inspection; covered by x402Enforcement.spec
findings.remediation: None required. Keep x402Enforcement.spec as the guard.
findings.residual_risk: A staging deployment without enforcement returns simulated successes, by design.

findings.title: Review notes on uncommitted /api/payouts/batch (another session's work)
findings.description: Authenticated (requireUser) and rate-limited; creates pending_signature payment intents only, so no broadcast or settlement bypass. Notes for its owner, unvalidated: (1) response field estimatedGasSavingsVsSwiftUsd assumes $25 per SWIFT payment, an invented figure in an API response; (2) intents are created with Promise.all, so one failing line leaves earlier lines created (non-atomic batch); (3) body read with req.json() + safeParse bypasses validateBody's 100KB cap; (4) audit log records recipient addresses; (5) no KYC tier/feature check, unlike other money routes; (6) route is unclassified in security/route-manifest.json (fails routeManifest.spec). Correct classification: USER.
